FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Mdmak Tech
FAQ.q1: How does Mdmak Tech connect contractors with suppliers in Saudi Arabia?
FAQ.a1: Mdmak Tech is a B2B procurement platform where contractors post RFQs, and verified suppliers submit competitive quotes. The platform streamlines the entire sourcing process — from posting requirements to comparing offers and awarding contracts — all in one place.
FAQ.q2: Is Mdmak Tech free to use?
FAQ.a2: Yes, contractors and suppliers can register and start using the platform for free. The Starter plan includes up to 5 RFQs per month with basic quotation features. For higher volumes and advanced features, we offer Pro and Enterprise plans.
FAQ.q3: What construction materials can I source through the platform?
FAQ.a3: You can request quotes for a wide range of construction materials including steel, cement, electrical supplies, paints, sanitary ware, HVAC systems, insulation, flooring, doors, and more. The platform supports all major categories used in Saudi construction projects.
FAQ.q4: How quickly do suppliers respond to RFQs?
FAQ.a4: Suppliers are notified instantly when a new RFQ is published. Response times vary, but most suppliers submit their offers within 24-48 hours. The platform sends automatic reminders as the deadline approaches to ensure competitive participation.
FAQ.q5: Can Mdmak Tech handle large-scale construction projects?
FAQ.a5: Absolutely. Mdmak Tech is built for projects of all sizes — from small renovations to large-scale commercial and infrastructure developments. The Enterprise plan includes ERP integration, dedicated account management, and advanced reporting for complex procurement needs.
FAQ.q6: How does Mdmak Tech ensure supplier quality?
FAQ.a6: All suppliers undergo a verification process including commercial registration (CR) and tax certificate validation. The platform also features a rating and review system where contractors rate suppliers after each completed order, building a transparent reputation system.

Shared.sset_desc: What the Sales module owns, what it reads from others, and what will never be built here
Shared.sset_step_1_body: Arrives from CRM only: a quote request for a client or prospect registered there. There is no direct door — a new party is registered in CRM first.
Shared.sset_step_1_guard: A request past its due date shows red · what we cannot price goes back with a factual reason — never an apology.
Shared.sset_step_2_body: Price comes from the client agreement, then the quantity tier, then the list; lead time from honest readiness. None of that lives in CRM, so pricing happens here — one record, not two copies.
Shared.sset_step_2_guard: A discount above the role's cap is blocked · selling below cost is blocked for every role.
Shared.sset_step_3_body: You type in the form and it appears at once on an official document under the company's letterhead and VAT number — lines, discount, amount in words, payment schedule and terms — printable or saved as PDF. Then you log that it was sent, and validity starts.
Shared.sset_step_3_guard: Issuing locks the figures · sending locks the whole document · any later change is a revision carrying the base number and a suffix.
Shared.sset_step_4_body: The client's acceptance turns the quote into an order with a frozen price and a delivery promise. The opportunity closes as won in CRM, and the win rate is computed from quote outcomes, never typed.
Shared.sset_step_4_guard: No order without an accepted quote · the promise is never earlier than the earliest honest readiness.
Shared.sset_step_5_body: Written in the quote and carried to the order as the client accepted it: instalments with their percentages. Anything made to order is not quoted without an advance before production — the same rule Manufacturing enforces.
Shared.sset_step_5_guard: No invoice and no receipt here · the advance blocks reservation and execution until Finance confirms the deposit — not until the client says "I paid".
Shared.sset_step_6_body: When you report the advance to Finance, the production request for the shortfall reaches the plant as "awaiting Finance": it plans but does not execute. Once Finance confirms, the plant answers with a work order or a reasoned decline.
Shared.sset_step_6_guard: No reservation or execution before Finance confirms the advance · the plant's response clock starts after confirmation.
Shared.sset_step_7_body: A made-to-measure product does not enter production before the measurement is recorded, and a drawn product is not cut before the client approves. Manufacturing records the measurement and we only nudge; the client's approval is ours to chase and record.
Shared.sset_step_7_guard: While either gate is closed, readiness is not computed at all.
Shared.sset_step_8_body: The work order moves through the stations, and what is finished enters the warehouse as stock that Inventory owns.
Shared.sset_step_8_guard: Scheduling and priority are the plant's call — we read the ready date and never book capacity.
Shared.sset_step_9_body: The three-step handshake: issue request → Inventory authorises → the client signs for the quantity actually received, which may differ from the request — and value follows it.
Shared.sset_step_9_guard: A quantity above truly-available stock is blocked · a shipment held by Finance does not leave until released.
Shared.sset_step_10_body: When the client tells you they paid an instalment, you report it to Finance with the amount, transfer date, bank reference and the receipt if there is one. That is your whole part in the money.
Shared.sset_step_10_guard: We issue no invoice and record no receipt · nothing changes on the order before Finance answers.
Shared.sset_step_11_body: Finance matches the deposit against the bank statement and answers: confirmed, or not found — the tax invoice and its posting are theirs alone.
Shared.sset_step_11_guard: "Not found" returns to us as a decision: check with the client and report again · "confirmed" on the advance releases the order.
Shared.sset_step_12_body: A return with its reason and disposition (back to stock, or scrapped); Finance settles it with a credit note.
Shared.sset_step_12_guard: No return on an unsigned shipment — the delivered quantity is corrected instead of inventing a return.
Shared.sset_rule_body: A module owns the record whose lifecycle it owns. The quote and its document, the order, the promise, the delivery and the transfer notice are Sales' · the invoice, verifying the deposit and the posting are Finance's · the request, the client and the opportunity are CRM's · scheduling and measurement are Manufacturing's · stock and its movement are Inventory's · company details and logo are Settings & Governance's. Whatever you see here from another module carries its source badge and is never edited from here.

Whoever stands at the delivery point records the receipt — the storekeeper or the site engineer — counting line by line and giving the reason for any reject; Finance pays only what was accepted.
